name: AI Energy Boom
description: Hypothesis scenario: no effective demand cap on energy — AI compute and robotics have near-unbounded appetite. Levers vs baseline (endogenous-rule era): AI cognitive labor payoff on (aiWorkerEquivalentPerTWh 1e5), low robot integration friction (robotIntegrationExponent 0.5, diffusion 0.30), and a datacenter spend ceiling 10x baseline (13% of GDP on total cost of ownership: power + capital service). ROBOT/DC CAPITAL RESCORE (November 2026): robot and chips+facility capex builds robot and datacenter capital stocks inside K and is added to general investment orders, competing for finance rather than for general capital's desired expansion; before, it froze general capital at ~$967T from 2049 (GDP 2100 ~$1,204T). The datacenter brake now prices total cost of ownership (capital at the lagged interest rate + 15% depreciation, plus power), so the ~18% return on capital this scenario reaches brakes its own buildout (power-bill brake: ~757k TWh and GDP ~$3,740T in 2100). DC capex (default $45B per average GW, calibrated to 2025 Dell'Oro capex) rises from ~$0.7T in 2025 to ~$46T in 2050, ~$95T in 2075 and ~$250T in 2100; datacenter capital reaches ~$1,220T of a ~$6,350T capital stock. Energy WACC reaches ~12.4% in 2075 and ~11.9% in 2100. Outputs reach GDP ~$3,175T, a labor share ~8%, robots ~1,530/1000 workers, datacenters ~252k TWh, emissions ~67 Gt/yr and warming ~3.3C in 2100. Treat this highly path-dependent upper envelope as a stress test, not a forecast; DC capacity rationing and dedicated lease/debt service remain unmodeled.
